substantive_insights: The main tension was between one person's routine (A cooking most nights) and others' practical needs (B's early shift, smell spread).
A simple rule tying responsibility to action ('whoever cooks washes pans' + use extractor/open window) addresses both cleanliness and smell, reducing friction.
Scheduling guaranteed 'late' slots is an effective compromise to share access to the stove while preserving A's preference to cook most nights.
Immediate mitigation (turning on extractor, washing pan) was necessary to resolve the acute problem even after scheduling was negotiated.
